Anthropic has released its latest AI model, Claude Opus 5.5. The new version comes roughly two months after the previous Opus model upgrade, in line with Anthropic's historical release cadence.

Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5

Anthropic's Claude series currently offers several AI models.

The three main models are Haiku (the smallest and cheapest), Sonnet (mid-sized and mid-priced), and Opus (the largest and most expensive of the three).

There is also Fable/Mythos, which offers greater capability at a higher cost and represents Anthropic's top tier.

This release upgrades the Opus model from version 5.0 to version 5.5.

Anthropic stated: "Opus 5.5 is the first model we are releasing after our call to slow down frontier development. As with previous models, it was tested by external evaluators prior to release, including METR and Frontier Design. In our most comprehensive alignment evaluations, it achieved the highest score to date."

The following is Anthropic's introduction to Opus 5.5's performance:

Regarding coding, Anthropic's introduction is as follows:

Opus 5.5 is particularly adept at handling lengthy, wide-ranging tasks such as codebase migrations and audits. One early tester used it to audit and fix a codebase of 200,000 lines in under three hours; the same work took Opus 5 over 20 hours and used 2.5x more tokens. In an internal test, we asked Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 to translate HAProxy, widely used software for balancing network traffic across servers, from C to Rust. Both rewrites passed nearly all of HAProxy's own regression tests, but Opus 5.5 completed the job in 9.5 hours while Fable 5.1 took 12 hours, and Opus 5.5 cost 51% less. Opus 5.5 reaches the frontier in agentic coding at lower cost. At FrontierCode's default effort level, it beats GPT-6 Astra at roughly 20% of the cost per task. On Terminal Bench 4.0, it ties Astra at about 40% of the cost; on CursorBench, it leads GPT-5.6 Sol by 11 points at about one-third of the cost.

In addition, pricing for Opus 5.5 has been adjusted compared with Opus 5:

Opus 5.5 requires fewer computational resources to run than Opus 5, and its pricing reflects this. Our tests show that, at default settings, the cost for typical workloads is 40% lower than Opus 5. Input and output tokens are priced at $4 and $20 per million respectively, 20% lower than Opus 5. Cache reads (which make up the bulk of the cost of agentic and coding work) are $0.20 per million tokens, 60% lower than Opus 5. Opus 5.5 also outputs more than 30% faster than Opus 5.

The new Claude Opus 5.5 model is available to try now. Looking ahead, Anthropic said the Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 models will be "released in the coming weeks, with the same improvements in performance, efficiency, and safety."

You can learn more about the new Claude Opus 5.5 model here.
